thread:
Maya: incoming page — canary pool in eu-west showing repeated OOMs and stuck requests, latency +40% on /v1/generate. incident-bot auto-paged oncall. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: P1 - Canary deploy anomaly detected (eu-west). Symptoms: memory spikes, request timeouts, kv_eviction stalls. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

Sam: seeing the same. logs show repeated: `kv_eviction: stuck_waiters=12` and `prefetch_writer: timed_out_trylock` across canary pods. Started ~5m after rollout began.

Lina: which feature flag rolled? could be the new prefetch path.

Sam: flag is `new-prefetch-v2` gated for canary. @deploy-bot can you flip it off for canary?

deploy-bot: ACK. Running: `ff-control kill new-prefetch-v2 --env=canary --actor=deploy-bot`

deploy-bot: success — flag off in canary. Waiting 30s for connections to quiesce.

John: I'll scale the canary pool up while we watch to reduce tail latency. Running: `kubectl scale deploy/canary-runtime -n inference-eu-west --replicas=8`

Maya: after scaling and flag flip, errors down a bit but latency has not fully recovered. Memory growth slowed but several pods still report long GC pauses. Might be safer to rollback the canary binary.

Priya: agree — prefer rollback to previous sha and collect heapdumps. Sam, do you have the previous SHA?

Sam: previous known-good is `sha-9f4d3a`. Initiating rollback:```
redwood deploy rollback --service=canary-runtime --to=sha-9f4d3a --wait
```

deploy-bot: Rollback started: step 1/3 draining new canary pods. Expect ~2-3 minutes.

incident-bot: Customer impact summary: ~12% of production requests routed through canary; error rate rose 0.1% -> 1.8% for EU region. No evidence of data corruption; errors are timeouts/503s.

Maya: please notify Support and Product: short status blurb to status page and notify priority customers in EU.

Sam: creating quick issue + collecting logs/heapdumps: RNW-5234. Attached preliminary heapdumps from two canary pods. Suspect concurrent writer race in prefetched KV index leading to deadlock under high prefetch concurrency.

John: rollback finished. Traffic baseline restored. Metrics: error rate back to 0.12%, p99 latency trending to normal.

Maya: confirmed. Rolling incident to monitoring state. We should still capture additional diagnostics before we consider the canary pipeline healthy.

Priya: follow-ups: enable heapdump-on-failure for next canary run, run smaller ramp (1% -> 5% -> 10%), and add a time-based watchdog for kv_eviction stalls.

Lina: taking oncall watch. I'm next on rotation; handoff note: rollback completed, monitoring stable, incident owner Sam (RNW-5234) for root cause/postmortem. I'll watch eu-west for 30m and escalate if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks @Lina. I've posted draft to status page: 'We experienced degraded response times and intermittent errors in EU related to a canary deployment. A rollback was performed; mitigating actions are complete. No customer data loss observed. Investigations continue.'

Priya: postmortem owner assigned to Sam. Sam — please include heapdumps, timing on prefetch writes, and traffic ramp overlap in RCA.

Sam: will do. quick note: adding eng-runtime and eng-ml to RNW-5234 for follow-up.

Maya: closing oncall thread — handoff done. Leaving channel. :wave:
